# Next-response log loss in ASSISTments skill-builder sequences

Freeze before opening official test outcomes. Use pyKT's ASSIST2015 split at ccbaf37b07e3e7ff7b2415475b2faacb967d54ea. Fit folds 1–4, select on fold 0. Score every response after the first per official test learner, with one vote per event in primary natural-log loss. Supply the current skill and all earlier recorded skills and responses. The estimand is conditional on reaching the next opportunity. A tutor's decision to continue a skill may carry information about mastery; it also limits transfer to a different practice policy.

Candidate combines the published pyKT DKT recurrent forecast with a gradient-boosted history forecast. The latter includes the current run of same-skill opportunities and correct/incorrect streaks within that run, plus log counts of preceding successes/failures for learner and current skill, total attempts, current skill identity, last same-skill response and event distance to previous same skill. Tree depth is controlled by 15 or 31 leaves, 200 iterations and learning rate .07. Choose by development loss separately for each feature set. Candidate is a probability blend with DKT weight chosen among 0,.25,.5,.75,1 on development loss. Include each full component alone, a tree omitting run and streak features, a blend using that tree, skill-conditional training mean with add-one smoothing, and a logistic regression with skill intercepts and the full numeric histories. The component comparisons test whether the models give complementary information. The matched blend tests whether streaks add value beyond flexible learner/skill counts. DKT uses the released pyKT LSTM class, hidden/embedding size 64, dropout .1, Adam .001, a maximum of 12 epochs, minimum development-loss checkpoint, seed 731. All methods share event IDs, inputs available at decision time, target and denominator. Clamp forecasts to [1e-7,1-1e-7] when scoring.

Stage one requires .015 nats or more in observed average improvement against each control and lower simultaneous 95% learner-cluster bootstrap endpoint above zero (5,000 paired draws with Bonferroni across six contrasts). Failure disqualifies this candidate. A surviving candidate proceeds to the original P05 comparator register including simpleKT, HawkesKT and LêFoKT on compatible inputs, and a second untouched release. This local protocol has no independent timestamp. The public cohort has been used by previous authors. A first-stage pass by itself adds zero verified papers.
